span.label: mechanisms
span.term: The feedforward sweeps triggered in turn by flankers and targets still carry only local contrast information, so motor activation is driven by raw local contrast while conscious brightness is settled later by recurrent interactions.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Response priming accesses a stimulus representation that precedes lightness constancy, i.e. one that has not yet discounted illumination.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Placing the high-luminance flanker on the lighted segment turns it into a local decrement (and the low-luminance flanker on the shadowed segment into a local increment), which is what inverts the priming sign.

span.label: **A QUALITATIVE DISSOCIATION, AND IT IS A REVERSAL RATHER THAN AN ATTENUATION:** `Quotation withheld.` Not a smaller effect in one condition - **the sign flips**, while the observer's own brightness match goes the other way. A quantitative dissociation can be argued about with a power analysis; a reversal cannot
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE CONTROL THAT MAKES THIS DIFFERENT IN KIND FROM EVERY OTHER DISSOCIATION IN THIS CORPUS:** `Quotation withheld, and it relies solely on characteristic differences in processing dynamics between the priming and matching tasks.` **dehaene1998 flashes a numeral for 43 ms between masks; marcel1983, holcomb2005 and Finkbeiner2011 all argue about whether the prime was seen. This paper lets the observer look straight at it.** So the gap is not between seen and unseen but between two live representations of one visible stimulus - which is a different claim, needing none of the machinery the awareness literature spends its credibility on
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **THE CLAIM IS A TRIPLE NEGATIVE THAT NAMES ITS WINNER:** `Quotation withheld` **The two excluded candidates are the physical variable and the perceptual variable** - between them, everything anyone would have guessed - and each was excluded by a measurement rather than by an argument. The third is named, and it is a property of the stimulus's relation to its own neighbourhood
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: **AND THE INFERENCE IS CAREFULLY PARTIAL:** `If priming effects are in systematic disagreement with the flankers' perceived brightness values, this suggests that AT LEAST SOME ASPECTS of lightness constancy are ABSENT FROM THE RESPONSE ACTIVATION PROCESS.` **`at least some aspects` and `suggests` are both in the quote**, and they are the difference between this and a claim that the motor pathway is pre-constancy. The illusion used here IS a consequence of lightness constancy - the authors say so - so its failure to reach the response is evidence about one pathway, not a map of the visual system
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: local luminance contrast —causes→ response priming
span.note: direction on the measure: increases · strength of the relation: 0.95 — **`EXCLUSIVELY` IS IN THE QUOTE AND IT IS THE WHOLE CLAIM.** Two rival causes are named and excluded in the same sentence - physical luminance and subjective brightness - so this is not `X is associated with Y` but `X and not the two things you would have guessed`. Weight 0.95: the general discussion's opening sentence, resting on a systematic variation of the illusion rather than on one contrast. `increases` means more local contrast in the priming direction yields more priming, and the reversal condition is the same relation with the contrast sign flipped.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: response priming —distinct-from→ subjective brightness
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.95 — **A REVERSAL, NOT AN ATTENUATION, AND THAT IS WHY THIS EARNS 0.95.** `distinct-from` usually records that two concepts are not the same thing; here the quote shows them moving in OPPOSITE directions on the same stimulus - one flanker appears brighter and primes as if darker. **And the second sense is what makes it valuable: no masking, no brief presentation, the stimuli in plain view.** Every other dissociation in this corpus separates a seen thing from an unseen thing; this separates two representations of a thing the observer is looking at.
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: When the illusion made the two flankers look similar in brightness, the priming effect reversed sign: consistent flankers slowed responses and inconsistent flankers speeded them.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The same flanker could look brighter than its partner while priming the response assigned to the darker stimulus.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Brightness matching never reversed: the physically more luminant flanker was always judged the brighter one in every illusion condition.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Varying the light-to-shadow ratio showed that priming flipped sign in exactly the conditions where each flanker's contrast against its own background flipped from increment to decrement.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The reversal survived when targets were made all-decrement or all-increment pairs, so participants could not have been responding to target contrast sign alone.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Overall, response priming tracked neither the flankers' physical luminance nor their perceived brightness, but only their local luminance contrast against the immediately surrounding background.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The priming-perception dissociation was obtained with all stimuli fully visible, without masking or brief presentation.
